newsitem.title: ITALY: Only one in six Italy provincial elections decided.
newsitem.headline: Only one in six Italy provincial elections decided.

text.p: A centre-left candidate for president of the provincial government of Ravenna won in the first round of Italian local elections on Monday but the other five provincial races will have to be decided in a May 11 runoff.
In all six provincial contests, candidates of the Northern League failed to achieve first or second place and were thrown out of the running.
The League lost the presidency of the provincial governments it held in its headquarters, Mantua, as well as in Gorizia and Pavia.

Gabriele Albonetti, who was backed by the Olive Olive Tree coalition and the hard-left Communist Refoundation, won in Ravenna, with about 65.8 pct of the votes, with nearly all of the ballots counted.
In Mantua, centre-left candidate Tiziana Gualtieri in Ferri took 43.4 percent. She will face Augusto Manerba, who won 24.2 percent.
In Pavia, centre-right candidate Silvio Beretta won 36.7 percent against about 25.0 percent for Cesare Bozzano of the centre-left.
In Gorizia, leftist Giorgio Brandolin won 44.9 percent against 39.6 percent for Antonio Devetag of the centre-right.
In the Tuscan city of Lucca, Guido Moutier of the centre right won 46.5 percent, just head of leftist candidate Andrea Tagliasacchi, with 46.4 percent.
In Viterbo, just north of Rome, the centre-right's Giulio Marini won 46.7 percent, ahead of Ugo Nardini of the centre-left who won 35.4 percent. -- Rome newsroom +396-678-2501
